faqs.q: Someone photographed an iguana in Vero Beach — do we have an iguana problem?
faqs.a: Not in the South Florida sense. On the Treasure Coast, iguanas are at report level: scattered sightings, often traced to released or escaped pets, without the established breeding colonies of Broward or Miami-Dade. Report a sighting to FWC's exotic species line, photograph it, and do not approach it. If one takes up residence on your property, removal on your land with your authorization is lawful and the animal may never be released — but be wary of anyone selling Vero a Miami-style iguana program; the population here does not justify it.

Vero Beach.wildlife_intro:
Vero Beach splits between the barrier island — Riomar, John's Island, the beachside streets under live-oak canopy — and the mainland's citrus-era neighborhoods and newer western subdivisions. Island work is salt-grade exclusion for roof rats and raccoons in high-value homes; mainland work leans agricultural, with armadillos in the grove-edge yards and opossums everywhere. Iguana reports on the island are exactly that — reports: Vero sits in the Treasure Coast report-level zone, where a sighting gets documented and FWC notified, not marketed as an established-colony removal.

The oak canopy of Old Riomar and McAnsh Park is Vero's squirrel and rat highway, and our island inspections are canopy-led. Mainland, the inspections follow the groves: packing sheds, grove-edge houses, and the canal banks of the Indian River Farms grid. Gopher tortoises occupy mainland sand ridges; their burrows are identified and buffered everywhere we work in this county.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Sebastian?

faqs.q: A bobcat crosses my Sebastian Highlands yard — is that a problem?
faqs.a: Almost never. Bobcats patrol the Highlands' vacant lots hunting rabbits and rodents, and a sighting at dawn is the grid working as habitat. Florida law treats bobcats narrowly: they are excluded from general nuisance take except when causing or about to cause property damage or a safety threat, and a live-captured bobcat must be released, never euthanized. Secure poultry and small pets at night, and the bobcat is free rodent control. Damage situations get an honest assessment and, where the law requires it, an FWC conversation.

Sebastian.wildlife_intro:
Sebastian is a river town — the St. Sebastian River, the lagoon, Pelican Island just offshore — with a fishing-town core, the Sebastian Highlands' vast platted grid, and grove and marsh country around it. The Highlands' empty lots are the wildlife engine: raccoons, armadillos, tortoises, and bobcats use the undeveloped grid, and the built streets inherit the traffic. Riverfront and lagoon homes get dock raccoons, roof rats in the palms, and wading birds as scenery.

Highlands inspections account for the lot next door: vacant land raises the sealing standard, because pressure is constant. We also walk Sebastian's older river cottages gently — aging roofs and additions need fitted work, not force. Pelican Island's protected status sets the town's tone: the birds are the point here, and our role with any protected species is identification and referral, from tortoises on land to rookery birds on the river.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Fellsmere?
faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the home needs afterward. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins, with no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: What is digging the small sand mounds in my Fellsmere yard?
faqs.a: That depends on the shape. Eastern moles leave raised surface tunnels and small molehills, armadillos leave scattered digging in beds and lawn edges, and in sandy north and central Florida soils a southeastern pocket gopher leaves a row of sand mounds. A large burrow with a wide, half-moon apron of sand is different — that is likely a gopher tortoise burrow, which is protected, carries a 25-foot permit buffer, and must be left alone. Call us and describe the digging and we will identify it before any work is planned.

Fellsmere.wildlife_intro:
In Fellsmere, our crew's steady calls are raccoons in attics and chimneys, eastern gray squirrels at soffits and gable vents, and roof rats moving from palms and fruit trees onto rooflines. Opossums and striped skunks work yards after dark, armadillos dig lawns and beds, eastern moles tunnel the sandy ground, and Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats roost in older rooflines through the warm months. The county's habitat — barrier-island beach towns, citrus country inland, and lagoon-front suburbs — and features such as Indian River Lagoon, Sebastian Inlet State Park, St. Sebastian River Preserve, Pelican Island National Wildlife Refuge keep that pressure close to housing in every season.

Florida has no winter shutdown for this work, so Fellsmere jobs run year-round, with the one hard legal gate being bats: exclusion is legal only from August 15 through April 15, and maternity-season bat calls become inspection and scheduling. Our crew works under FWC Rule 68A-9.010 with the property owner's authorization — Florida issues no nuisance-trapper license — checks any live trap at least every 24 hours, and seals the entry as part of the job so the next animal cannot use the same opening. Call us at (844) 544-3498 and tell us what you are hearing or seeing.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Gifford?
faqs.a: Gifford quotes are sized to the homes: modest houses, honest figures, written after inspection, with the addition-junction sealing that older construction needs itemized plainly — no beachside pricing transplanted to a mainland block.

faqs.q: Rats come from the grove behind my Gifford home — can sealing really help?
faqs.a: Yes, because grove rats still need a way in. Roof rats live in the citrus and commute to attics for shelter; a sealed roofline breaks the commute even when the grove population stays high. We trap the animals inside, seal every entry with gnaw-proof flashing, and recommend clearing fallen fruit within the yard's edge. You cannot trap a grove empty, and we will not sell that — but a closed house stays closed while the grove does what groves do.

Gifford gets the same inspection-first service as the beachside, priced for its housing: older block and frame homes, many with additions, where the entries are at the junctions between old and new construction. faqs.a: Winter Beach quotes come from one property walk covering house and outbuildings, priced in writing by structure and problem — small-community math, with no upsell toward programs the acreage does not need.

faqs.q: Sandhill cranes keep coming into our Winter Beach yard — are they protected?
faqs.a: Fully. The Florida sandhill crane is State Threatened; harming one, or feeding one, is illegal, and removal is not a service. Cranes in a Winter Beach yard are hunting insects and grubs in wet ground and usually move through seasonally. Deterrents that help: motion sprinklers, no seed or pet food outside, and patience during the weeks colts are learning to forage. An injured crane is an FWC or wildlife-rehabilitator call — we will give you the direction, not a trap.

It is quiet, rural-suburban, and wildlife-rich: raccoons, armadillos, and opossums around the acreage homes, roof rats in the grove-side houses, and sandhill cranes and wading birds in the wet pastures. Gopher tortoises hold the sandy ridges.

Winter Beach service is country service — property walks, outbuilding checks, burrow identification, and attic work for the older homes, in one visit. Crane conflicts are deterrence-only. Hog sign at a property edge gets a referral to licensed hog trappers who specialize in it; we will not pretend a yard-trap program answers a sounder. Honest scoping is the product in a community this small, where our reputation travels by name.
